Commentary.Commentary: Okay then. Time for some break. I badly need some coffee. Australia have got some score on the board. The pitch looks flat but there is bounce. Not much turn. 232 should not be too much of a headache of a chase but if the Aussies can get de Kock and du Plessis before the score touches 100, well, you never know... Join us back at 6.05 pm local (0735 GMT).

Time for a Chris Lynn interview. The Australian T20 star admits that the batting display is very disappointing as the batsmen could not convert their starts. Feels that the Aussies are 50 runs short but also hopes that his team has a good bowling attack and wants them to start well. On getting dismissed by Rabada, Chris says that he tried to get the wood over the Protea but unfortunately could not. On the send-off, Lynn is not too perturbed and puts it down to part and parcel of the game. Adds further that if Rabada does come out to bat, then Starc and Hazlewood will remind him in their style though.

Dwaine Pretorius feels that the South African bowlers bowled pretty well, adjusting to the lines and lengths. On making it to the World Cup squad, Pretorius says that one just needs to perform and the other things can take care of themselves. On his knee injury, Dwaine recounts it as a very tough experience and feared that his cricketing career would be over. Is happy that he is fit now and can play.

When you pick 5 bowlers in your side, your bowling needs to perform. And it did again, for South Africa. Dale Steyn did not strike early on but was economical. Lungi Ngidi had a bad outing and for a second, it seemed like Kagiso Rabada would too, but he came back strongly to finish with a 4-fer. However, the pick of the bowlers was Dwaine Pretorius, who ran through the middle order, getting Finch, Maxwell and Stoinis, leaving Australia with no power hitters at the death. Here he is, having a chat.

Same old story for Australia. None of the openers batting long and no one from the middle order gutsing it out. Alex Carey tried to do that today but he got run out of partners. All the batsmen were trying to bash the ball almost every time, trying to get to 300 or 350 and have fallen well short.

Then, came a period where Lynn cut loose. He smashed Kagiso Rabada for 18 runs in 4 balls but eventually, the latter had his revenge. That, was the turning point. Australia slipped from 133/3 to 170/6 and kept on losing momentum, before the last-wicket pair gave some respect to the total.

Well, that is some sort of a recovery from the Aussie tail but they are at least 30-40 runs short. The partnership between Shaun Marsh and Aaron Finch seemed to be showing control and then Finch and Lynn showed patience. But, the middle order gave it away.

NOT OUT! Impact is umpire's call! The Australian skipper heaves a huge sigh of relief. Tell you, that was very, very close. On a length outside off, coming back in, Finch looked to defend and the ball went to point. Pretorius appealed but the umpire turned it down. The bowler was confident that the ball hit the pad first and skipper Faf du Plessis went with his young bloke. Review time. Hawk Eye shows the impact to be very, very marginal! To the naked eye, in the replays, without Hawk Eye, that looked to be hitting in line...
Okay... what do we have here? Pretorius reckons that he has Finch LBW and Faf has taken the review. Looks close. Where is the impact?

Did not review one in Perth when he should have and now, agreed with Head to review one when he should have let it be. Early strike again for South Africa.
South Africa are tightening their lines and lengths. They were a bit awry in the first 2 overs but they are learning now.

Again on a good length on off stump, Finch tried to play but gets beaten.
Good length delivery on off stump, Finch cuts it towards point.

FOUR! FANTASTIC! Boy, the local lad is up and running. Half volley outside off, Head leans into the shot and drives it through the covers for a boundary! 10 runs from that over, which could have had a wicket too!

RUN OUT CHANCE MISSED! Ohh... David Miller nearly pulled off another one, like he did at the WACA. Finch worked this towards mid-wicket and set off for a quick single. David Miller charged on to the ball from short mid-wicket and then had an under-arm flick at the bowler's end, only to miss. The Aussie skipper was a goner.
Down the leg side, Travis misses his tuck and the ball goes off his pads through fine leg. A leg bye taken.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Fine way to get off the mark! On a length outside off, Head punches this on the up through the covers and gets a boundary!
Lungi Ngidi to bowl with the second new ball.
Full on off stump, the batsmen drives it towards covers.
HUGE APPEAL FOR LBW FROM THE BOWLER! Good length delivery into middle stump, Aaron gets hit on the pads but umpire shakes his head. Probably height was the issue.
Full and outside off, AF looks to drive but the ball goes off the outside edge, past second slip, towards third man. Two runs taken to get Australia underway.
Bowls short outside off stump, Aaron lets it go.
Bowls on a good length, Finch hits it straight towards the bowler.
Bowls on a good length on leg stump, Finch pushes it to mid-wicket.
We are ready for the game to begin. Like the last game, Dale Steyn will start off the proceedings. Travis Head and Aaron Finch to open again for Australia. Here we go!

TEAM CHANGES - Australia have made two changes to their side - Shaun Marsh and Adam Zampa come in place of D'Arcy Short and Nathan Coulter-Nile. South Africa have made one change - Dwayne Pretorius replaces Andile Phehlukwayo.
Toss - South Africa have won the toss and chosen to field first. So once again, the Aussie batsmen will be under pressure to put a huge total on board.

Hello and a warm welcome to the 2nd ODI between Australia and South Africa in Adelaide. The visitors would be looking to finish the series today by winning this match. On the other hand, the Kangaroos would look to end their losing rut, having lost 7 ODIs in a row. Interestingly, the last ODI which Australia won, was at the Adelaide Oval itself, earlier this year against England. The Proteas' bowling is again going to be the talking point in this match. The hosts would be looking to improve their batting and score big if they are put in to bat first. Hopefully, we get a contest.
